summary: Four inactive proofs reconstruct smooth proper Hessian existence, uniform smooth admissible approximation of continuous potentials, sharp uniform stability of proper solutions, and smoothness of continuous admissible weak solutions for 2<=m<n on a strictly positive Hermitian background. A penalty construction uses only a smooth Newton-form linear maximum principle; positive exponential coefficient a is reduced to coefficient one by scaling the metric and potential. The continuous viscosity version of TWWY Theorem 3.4 applies directly to the reconstructed limit, avoiding a second auxiliary family. Continuous Hessian products and strict domination remain explicitly declared primary inputs; general bounded-solution continuity is not asserted.

mathematical_checks: Smooth coefficient-one existence closes by 600+596, real elliptic extension 603, TWWY regularity and the invertible L-1 continuity path.
Metric/potential scaling reduces every positive exponential coefficient to one with an exact a^n cancellation.
The penalty obstacle density b is positive even if its smooth obstacle is inadmissible; admissibility at a positive maximum follows from cone monotonicity.
At the maximum against the continuous weak potential, the Newton-form linear upper-test condition gives d_N >= (N+1)^(-m), yielding the explicit global approximation error.
The smooth proper solution map is one-Lipschitz for the uniform norm of its prescribed exponent.
Continuous exponential uniqueness identifies the auxiliary limit before the trace estimate is applied.
The fixed smooth comparison and the trace/blowup constants are independent of every derivative of the approximating potential.
TWWY Theorem 3.4 and its continuous-viscosity extension match the global concave extension exactly; no full real Hessian bound or second auxiliary family is required.
Schauder bootstrapping is applied to the original smooth root operator on the compact interior cone set.
